messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High rate of CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS on gpu-pool-7 (us-west-2). Error rate spike started ~5m ago. Related metric: gpu-errs/cuda_illegal_address > 50/min. Auto-escalation to #incidents triggered.

alex: seeing repeated illegal-address faults from two hosts: gpu-node-7a and gpu-node-7c. Stack trace indicates A->B kernel hop during model reload. sample log: 
```
E CUDA: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS addr=0x7fffc1234f0 kernel=triton_exec.c +0x2f3
E NVRM: Xid (79) 00000004 0000ffff 00000000 00000000 0x0000 0x0000
```

maya: confirmed. traces show misaligned page table entries right before the crash. dmesg on gpu-node-7a: 
```
[ 1234.567890] iommu: unmap failed for 0x7fffc0000000
[ 1234.567891] NVIDIA: GPU page fault: 0x7fffc1234f0
```

sre_oncall: I'm going to cordon + drain the two affected nodes to stop further impact. tagging dev-runtime for kernel/driver analysis.

dev-runtime: ack. please drain with --delete-local-data and keep pods on fallback pool. Also enable model-variant-fallback for the overloaded routes. Suggest temporary routing: route traffic from gpu-pool-7 -> fallback-dedicated-cpu (quantized) for 10% then escalate.

ops-bot: COMMAND: kubectl cordon gpu-node-7a && kubectl drain gpu-node-7a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force

jen: doing cordon/drain now on 7a. starting 7c next. will keep you posted. :white_check_mark:

alex: running a small repro with the offending model in staging. it repros when concurrent reloads + >1 queued request happen. looks like an allocator race in our custom kernel-level page table ops.

karthik: quick diagnostic steps I ran: pulled coredump, ran addr2line on backtrace, compared kernel modules (nvidia/driver 525.60 vs 525.85 on other nodes). diff shows different module build flags.

ryan: from customer side: we're seeing error responses 1.8% across us-west-2 routes. three customers reported increased 500s: acme-inc, buildly, docsly. SLO alert page already created.

maya: workaround applied: pinned model reloads to single thread and disabled hot-reload for the affected variant. that immediately reduced reproducer frequency in staging.

dev-runtime: next actions: 1) keep nodes cordoned until we patch module or replace driver, 2) roll affected pods to other pools (fallback), 3) collect NVidia driver logs + kernel oops for postmortem.

jen: rolling restart of affected daemonsets in fallback pool to absorb load. routing change: increased fallback pool weight to 25% for 15m.

incident-bot: NOTE: customer-impact channel updated. Incident severity set to Sev2.

alex: uploaded tarball with /var/log/nvidia-installer.log, dmesg, and coredumps to S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/2359998888-gpu7a.tgz 

karthik: tried quick driver upgrade on a spare node (525.60 -> 525.85) and the repro didn't trigger in 2h. not a definitive fix but promising. planning to push a staged driver upgrade to 3 spare nodes then rotate.

sre_oncall: timeline & customer comms: 1) immediate mitigation — drained 7a/7c, switched 25% traffic to fallback models (done) 2) medium — staged driver upgrade & kernel module rebuild (in progress) 3) long — root cause fix in kernel-level page table ops + add guard rails to reload path.

ryan: I'll draft a short customer-facing blurb: "We're investigating an elevated GPU error rate in us-west-2 affecting a small percentage of requests. We are routing traffic to fallback capacity while we remediate. Some customers saw increased 500s. We'll follow up with a postmortem."

dev-runtime: action items (assigned): alex - reproduce & minimal repro + submit kernel patch MR; maya - gather full kernel oops & nvidia logs, upload to S3; karthik - staged driver upgrade plan and validation; jen - coordinate node rotations and verify cluster stability; ryan - customer comms.

jen: note: some downstream pods reported ephemeral OOM during drain; I increased horizontal-pod-autoscaler max to absorb traffic.

alex: got a partial patch to add an iova alignment check. will open MR with tests in ~2h.

ops-bot: METRIC: gpu-errs/cuda_illegal_address dropped from 65/min -> 8/min after routing change and drains.

sre_oncall: closing the real-time incident channel once driver rollouts complete and errors stay <5/min for 30m. scheduled postmortem for tomorrow 11:00am PT.

karthik: ack. adding checklist for postmortem: kernel oops timeline, driver build diffs, scheduler concurrent reload telemetry, impact by customer, remediation timeline.

ryan: thanks team. keeping on-call looped. I'll publish the customer note after patch validation. :thumbsup:
